content:
Austin is known for keeping it weird, but some of the city's residents have been keeping it weird for centuries!

For 30 years, locally owned Austin Ghost Tours has been uncovering the chilling stories, mysterious legends, and supernatural sightings hiding right here in Central Texas.

Tour guide and paranormal researcher Monica Ballard joined Sierra and Trevor on We Are Austin to share some of the city's spookiest secrets, reveal lesser-known haunted locations, and celebrate three decades of exploring Austin's supernatural history.

What makes Austin so haunted?

According to Ballard, Austin's unique geography and historic architecture make it a fascinating setting for paranormal activity.

"It's the way it's situated and what it's built out of," Ballard explained. "A lot of the buildings are built out of limestone, which is a great energy conductor. There are underground artesian springs under the city."

Ballard believes the combination of historic buildings, nearby water, and the energy of a bustling city creates the perfect environment for ghostly encounters.

Austin's lesser-known haunted locations

While many Austinites are familiar with the ghost stories surrounding the Driskill Hotel, Ballard says there are plenty of other mysterious locations worth exploring.

One of her favorites is the former Carmelo's Restaurant building on Fifth Street, which she associates with the spirit of Annie Pressler.

"It's a very haunted spot," Ballard shared.

She also highlighted several historic buildings designed by architect Abner Cook, including the Governor's Mansion, Pease Mansion, and Neill-Cochran House Museum.

Other locations on her haunted list include the Stephen F. Austin Hotel and Chateau Bellevue, home of the Austin Woman's Club.

For Ballard, these tours offer more than spooky stories. They're also an opportunity to discover the history hiding in plain sight.

"It's really amazing how many locals go on our tour and say, 'I've passed by that building many times and knew nothing about it, much less its haunted history.'"

30 years of ghost stories and paranormal investigations

Austin Ghost Tours is celebrating its 30th anniversary, continuing its tradition of introducing locals and visitors to the city's mysterious past.

In addition to guided walking tours, the company offers paranormal investigations for those interested in exploring unexplained activity.

Ballard is also sharing more of her experiences in her new book, "True Haunted Tales of Austin & Central Texas."

The book follows her earlier work, True Haunted Tales of the Driskill Hotel, and expands beyond Austin to include stories from Goliad, Bartlett, and other Central Texas communities.

"I really wanted to tell a lot about the adventures that Austin Ghost Tours has had, not just in Austin, but other places like Goliad and Bartlett," Ballard explained.

She says sharing these stories has inspired others to come forward with their own experiences.

"The moment that we keep these stories as ours and too close to ourselves, we never get anything new. So once we put them out there, that space is filled with more stories," Ballard shared, recalling advice from the company's owner.

Experience Austin's haunted history

Whether you're a paranormal enthusiast, history lover, or simply looking for a spooky Halloween adventure, Austin Ghost Tours offers a unique way to explore the city.

Halloween tours are available, and the company offers experiences throughout the year.
